## Statement

Lebesgue's **Dominated Convergence Theorem (DCT)** gives a sufficient condition
for exchanging limits and integrals. If a sequence of functions is **bounded in
absolute value by an integrable function** and **converges pointwise (almost
everywhere)**, then the integral of the limit is the limit of the integrals,
and the convergence even holds in $L^1$.

:::{.theorem data-title="Dominated Convergence Theorem"}

Let $(X,\mathcal{M},\mu)$ be a measure space and $f_{n}:X \to [-\infty, \infty]$
measurable functions such that the pointwise limit
$f(x)=\lim_{ n \to \infty }f_{n}(x)$ exists ($\mu$-almost everywhere). Assume
there is an integrable $g:X \to [0,\infty]$ with $\lvert f_{n} \rvert\leq g$
for each $n$. Then $f$ and every $f_n$ are integrable, and
$$
\lim_{ n \to \infty }\int_{X}f_{n}~d\mu=\int_{X}\lim_{ n \to \infty } f_{n}~d\mu=\int_{X}f~d\mu,
\qquad\lim_{n\to\infty}\int_X|f_n-f|\,d\mu=0.
$$

:::

:::{.proof}

Since $|f|\leq g$ and $|f_n|\leq g$, all these functions are integrable. As
$g+f_{n}\geq 0$ and $g-f_{n}\geq 0$, [[fatou-lemma]] gives
$$
\begin{align}
\int (g+f)\,d\mu & \leq \liminf_{n \to \infty}\int (g+f_{n})\,d\mu, \\
\int (g-f)\,d\mu & \leq \liminf_{n \to \infty}\int (g-f_{n})\,d\mu.
\end{align}
$$
Subtracting the finite quantity $\int g\,d\mu$ yields
$$
\int f\,d\mu\leq\liminf_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\,d\mu,\qquad
\int f\,d\mu\geq\limsup_{n\to\infty}\int f_n\,d\mu,
$$
so the limit exists and equals $\int f\,d\mu$. For the $L^1$ statement apply
this to $|f_n-f|\leq 2g$, which tends to $0$ pointwise.

:::

## Random Variables

Taking $\mu=\mathbb{P}$ we obtain the version for expectations.

:::{.theorem data-title="Dominated Convergence Theorem (Random Variables)"}

Let $\{ X_{n} \}$ be random variables with $X_n\to X$ almost surely, and
suppose $\lvert X_{n} \rvert\leq Y$ for every $n$ with
$\mathbb{E}Y<\infty$. Then $X$ is integrable and
$$
\lim_{n \to \infty}\mathbb{E}[X_{n}]=\mathbb{E}\left[\lim_{n\to \infty} X_{n}\right]=\mathbb{E}[X].
$$

:::

The assumption can be weakened to convergence in probability.

:::{.theorem data-title="DCT with Convergence in Probability"}

Assume $X_{n}\stackrel{\mathbb{P}}{\to}X$ and $|X_{n}|\leq Y$ with
$\mathbb{E}[Y]<\infty$. Then $\mathbb{E}[X_{n}] \to \mathbb{E}[X]$.

:::

:::{.proof}

Some subsequence converges to $X$ almost surely, so $|X|\leq Y$ a.s. and $X$ is
integrable. Suppose $\mathbb{E}X_n\not\to\mathbb{E}X$. Then there are
$\epsilon>0$ and a subsequence $n_k$ with
$|\mathbb{E}X_{n_k}-\mathbb{E}X|>\epsilon$. Since $X_{n_k}\to X$ in
probability, it has a further subsequence converging almost surely, along
which the DCT gives $\mathbb{E}X_{n_{k_j}}\to\mathbb{E}X$, a contradiction.

:::
